title: Riot Platforms signs a $9.1B, 20-year compute deal with Anthropic — completing the pivot from bitcoin miner to AI landlord
subtitle: Riot's Rockdale, Texas campus will host 191 megawatts of dedicated Anthropic capacity through June 2048, with two five-year options that could take the contract's total value to roughly $16.1B.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Riot Platforms confirmed on August 11 a $9.1B, 20-year compute agreement with Anthropic covering 191 megawatts at its Rockdale, Texas campus. The base contract runs through June 2048; two optional five-year extensions would lift the total to roughly $16.1B. Buildout is staged — 96 MW live by December 2027, the full 191 MW by June 2028 — and Anthropic will be the sole tenant. Riot's stock jumped double-digits on the confirmation and drew a wave of 'transformational' notes from sell-side analysts.

The deal completes a story that has been unfolding for two years. Riot spent 2024 and most of 2025 rebranding as an 'energy infrastructure' company, hedging its exposure to bitcoin's price cycle by leasing grid-connected megawatts to any tenant that would pay a stable long-term rate. AI training was the obvious destination, and the ERCOT interconnect queue in Texas — which has been under increasing scrutiny from state regulators over residential rate impacts — made already-connected miner sites some of the fastest-to-deploy AI capacity in the country. Riot is not the first miner to make the switch, but at this size it is now the largest by contract value.

For Anthropic, this is the third infrastructure announcement in eight days. It follows the August 6 $10B Volta/Bitdeer arrangement in Norway and the August 10 Theseus joint venture with Macquarie and GIC — three different financing shapes for capacity that together suggest a company treating compute allocation as a portfolio problem rather than a single vendor choice. The reported total across recent commitments is now approaching $71B, and separate reporting indicates Anthropic has also agreed to buy roughly $45B of capacity from xAI. The pattern is a lab locking in multi-gigawatt supply well ahead of Nvidia's next-generation allocations closing.

For learners: the AI power story is now inseparable from the AI model story. When you see a big lease or acquisition, read the small print — what's the megawatt count, where does the power actually come from, and who bears the cost when the local grid needs upgrading. Compute that looks abundant on a data-center brochure can be constrained in practice by a single substation approval. The frontier labs that finish 2026 in the strongest position will be the ones that treated the electricity supply chain as a first-class engineering problem, not an accounting one.
